notes: Summary: Mid-market analytics SaaS. Started with Hosted API trial, business wants predictable economics -> evaluating Dedicated for production.
Workload mix: primary = support chat (session-based, stateful), secondary = doc-search/semantic search (embeddings + rerank), occasional batch reranking jobs.
Trial results (hosted API): average request token mix: 80% generation (chat) / 20% embeddings; median tokens per chat request ~420 (prompt+completion), 95th ~1,200 tokens.
Observed qps during trial: sustained 120 qps during business hours; peak bursts up to 800 qps for <10 minutes (spike from product experiment).
Concurrency needs: typical concurrency ~35 sessions, p95 concurrency ~120 sessions during peak. Each session averages 8 requests/minute (short turns).
Latency targets: product needs p95 <= 500ms for chat interactions; current hosted p95 ~420ms on higher-tier model (good).
Throughput targets for Dedicated sizing: baseline commit target = 200 qps sustained; burst buffer to 1,000 qps for 15 mins; concurrency target p95 = 150.
Token mix for forecast: forecasted growth to 60% generation, 30% embeddings, 10% reranking within 12 months as features expand.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — they want clear cost per 1M tokens and breakeven vs hosted in 6-9 months. Interested in batching and quantization recommendations.
Security: Must support SSO (SAML), audit logging, KMS integration for keys, and US data residency for PII-heavy logs.
Deployment ask: Dedicated pool in us-east-1 with VPC peering to their prod VPC, private control plane preferred. Interested in option for on-prem later (air-gapped not required now).

POC takeaways: Hosted trial validated model quality and latency. Main unknowns: exact GPU count/instance types for Dedicated to hit 200 qps baseline with token mix, and autoscale policy to cover 1k qps burst economically.
AE notes: finance wants pricing scenarios: 1) reserved monthly commit (200 qps), 2) reserved + burst credits, 3) elastic Dedicated (pay-as-you-go) - show cost and ARR impact.
SE notes (Liam): recommend 2x gpus for baseline (est) + 4x for burst pool; need to run workload simulator with real token distributions. Requested load profile logs from trial team.
Customer quote: 'Hosted was great for deving, but we need predictable per-user latency and unit costs before GA.'
Next technical asks: capacity sizing doc w/ QPS->GPU mapping, expected latency vs concurrency curves, and recommended autoscale thresholds.
capacity_summary: PoC metrics attached: avg tokens/request=420, mean response latency=220ms, p95 latency=420ms (hosted), embeddings batch size avg=64
Suggested Dedicated sizing (initial): commit for 200 sustained QPS mapped to 2x A100-equivalent GPUs with optimized kernels + KV cache; burst pool 4x GPUs to handle 1k QPS spikes
Autoscale policy: scale up at sustained 250 qps for >5min, scale down after 10min below 180 qps. Keep 20% headroom for caching warmup.
Forecast notes: expected 30% traffic growth over 6 months; plan capacity re-eval at +50% traffic. Consider model variants: smaller model fallback for non-critical queries to reduce cost.
